scope: DBS (Dynamic Band Splitting) soundtrack separation into music, sound effects and speech: the two released models (JusperLee/DBS-TIGER-DnR, JusperLee/DBS-BSRNN-DnR), the ComfyUI pack hiroki-abe-58/ComfyUI-DBS, running it outside ComfyUI, hosted routes, what Fuobe has today, where DBS goes in Fuobe on both engines, and a build plan. Licences are information (owner's decision). Read-only: no code from these repositories was run or installed, nothing was installed into Fuobe's ComfyUI, and no paid API was called.

paper.title: Learning Where to Split: Dynamic Band Splitting for Audio Source Separation

code.licence: Apache-2.0 (THIRD_PARTY.md: MIT notices for BS-RoFormer, Music-Source-Separation-Training, TIGER/Look2Hear)

method: content-conditioned scorer rates every STFT bin inside 4 coarse regions
hard Top-K picks a fixed number of boundaries (128 band tokens)
content-weighted pooling makes one token per band
unchanged backbone (BSRNN, TIGER, BS-RoFormer or Mel-RoFormer) separates the tokens
tokens smoothed, expanded to the STFT grid, refined along frequency, decoded to complex masks by a frequency-shared head
DBS-MelRoFormer uses a soft router instead

io.mixtureConsistency: masks sum to 1+0j (dbs/modules/dbs.py L326-329): music + sfx + speech = input; max measured difference 5e-7 (VERIFICATION.md L56-57)
io.length: any; equal-weight overlap-add (dbs/engine/inference.py L29-53); clips <= half a window padded to one window, clips between half a window and one window run unpadded (L32-36)
io.auxOutput: model(mixture, return_aux=True) also returns the band boundaries (tiger.py L682-689); not exposed by the pack

stereoModes.mono: separates the channel mean (official usage); stems come out mono; 5.1 mean includes LFE and surrounds
stereoModes.each channel: separates every channel; time x channel count
stereoModes.fastStereoBed: proposal (guess until heard): separate the mono mean, AudioMerge(original, speech, subtract) broadcasts the mono speech over each channel and keeps the original stereo image (comfy_extras/nodes_audio.py L708-741); exact for centre-panned dialogue; AudioMerge divides the result by its peak when over 1.0 (L747-749)

quality.dataset: DnR v2 test set, 973 full-length tracks, SI-SDR dB
notes: abstract's 29.0% gain for DBS-BSRNN is vs the published BSRNN (9.07/7.03 = 1.290); vs retrained BSRNN(128) it is +18%
dialogue separates well (15-16 dB); music vs effects is weak (5.7-7.8 dB): expect bleed between those two stems
all numbers in-domain on synthetic English DnR v2; not measured on real films

packages.title: Split soundtrack in the Audio hub: dialogue, music and effects on both engines (and the DBS ground)
packages.brief:
GOAL. Give Fuobe a Split soundtrack tool in the Audio hub that turns any audio or video into Dialogue, Music, Effects and Music & effects stems on both engines, with a free live mixer, and lay the DBS ground every later package uses. Read docs/research/dbs-separation-7.md §1-§4, §6, §8 and §9 D1 first.

GROUND, OPEN ENGINE. (1) Pin the pack: add [ComfyUI-DBS]="https://github.com/hiroki-abe-58/ComfyUI-DBS f656e53434b5485c148a2866fbd6ddc6b6152ed6" to NODES in scripts/comfy/install-comfyui.sh (L15-34) with a comment that the Comfy Registry flags 0.1.0 (reason not public) and the code was read at this commit (§4.2). No extra Python packages (einops and safetensors are already installed). Add an opt-out block (DBS_WEIGHTS=0 skips it) that downloads config.json and model.safetensors of JusperLee/DBS-BSRNN-DnR @ 5af343f57f106fbb95efe8a60f1a3999eeb0aef8 and JusperLee/DBS-TIGER-DnR @ 22da7d4cd3ea63f9365181008bff1c0d2ab6fb2b into models/dbs/<name>/ and checks them with sha256sum -c against §3.1. (2) Library tooling (§4.5): KNOWN_MODELS entries keyed 'DBS-BSRNN-DnR/model.safetensors', 'DBS-BSRNN-DnR/config.json', 'DBS-TIGER-DnR/model.safetensors', 'DBS-TIGER-DnR/config.json' with folder 'dbs' and the pinned resolve URLs; a new spec field requiredModels handled in scripts/comfy/build-library.mjs beside the optionalModels loop (L335-346); the TIGER pair in optionalModels; packs: ['ComfyUI-DBS'] with PACK_CLASSES['ComfyUI-DBS'] = /^DBS(Loader|Separate)$/ (library.spec.mjs L140-143) and CUSTOM_NODE_REPOS (L110-136); new binding keys separationModel and channels in BINDING_KEYS (build-library.mjs L96ff) and the spec header. Presence then works as is: with the pack loaded, GET /models/dbs lists 'DBS-BSRNN-DnR/model.safetensors' etc., which /api/comfyui matches by file string. (3) Graph A separate-soundtrack-dbs exactly as §4.4 (hand-built JSON in scripts/comfy/hand-built/: LoadAudio -> DBSLoader -> DBSSeparate with output_sample_rate 'input' -> AudioMerge(original, speech, subtract) -> four SaveAudioAdvanced flac + PreviewAny report), outputs in order voice, music, effects, background, report; vramGb 0 with the note 'CPU OK, about 1.7 GiB on CUDA'; license text 'DBS weights Apache-2.0 (JusperLee; trained on DnR v2, CC BY 4.0); ComfyUI-DBS code MIT; vendored DBS code Apache-2.0 with MIT notices (BS-RoFormer, MSST, TIGER)'. Build it with npm run build -- separate-soundtrack-dbs in scripts/comfy so workflows/comfyui/manifest.json gets the entry. (4) ModelDef oss-dbs-separate in src/lib/catalog/models.ts next to oss-voice-separate (L1113): name 'DBS (dialogue, music, effects)', kind audio, tagline 'Splits a soundtrack into dialogue, music and effects · 23 MB · CPU or GPU · Apache-2.0', route comfy('separate-audio', 'separate-soundtrack-dbs', ...), options for the model (fast/best) and stereo stems. Map params to the bindings in src/server/providers/comfyui.ts: DBS-BSRNN-DnR unless GET /system_stats devices[0].type is 'cuda' (Fuobe already reads devices[0] at comfyui.ts L1530; ComfyUI server.py L783-796); 'mono' unless the user asks for stereo stems; 'each channel' for inputs with more than 2 channels (§4.4). (5) Stems: STEM_ALIASES (src/server/generations.ts L764) gains music: ['music'] and effects: ['effects','sfx']; STEM_ORDER (src/lib/catalog/payload.ts L822) gains 'music','sfx','effects' after the voice names; update the 'separate-audio' comment (src/lib/catalog/types.ts L59). Demo: src/server/providers/mock.ts L287-297 returns voice, music, effects and background demo WAVs (meta.stem) for oss-dbs-separate and for the cloud split. (6) Licences: a NODE_PACKS row pack('ComfyUI-DBS', 'https://github.com/hiroki-abe-58/ComfyUI-DBS/tree/f656e53434b5485c148a2866fbd6ddc6b6152ed6', { name: 'MIT', class: 'commercial', note: 'Dialogue / music / effects separation; MIT code, vendored DBS code Apache-2.0 with MIT notices; the DBS weights are Apache-2.0, trained on DnR v2 (CC BY 4.0)' }) in src/lib/licences.ts (~L406); the workflow license text gives the model rows; About & licences shows the DnR v2 CC BY 4.0 attribution (Petermann, Wichern, Wang, Le Roux) and the three MIT notices (§3.2).

GROUND, CLOUD ENGINE. Add sam-audio-separate through scripts/gen-cloud-models.py from the research row (paid-model-apis-3.json; fal-ai/sam-audio/separate; fields audio_url, prompt, acceleration, output_format 'wav'; pricing $0.05 per 30 s of output audio with a note that fal may bill the target and the residual both) and regenerate (pnpm gen:catalog). stemOutputs already tags target/residual and STEM_ALIASES maps them to voice/background.

packages.title: On this device (beta): DBS in the browser with ONNX and onnxruntime-web
packages.brief:
GOAL. Split a short clip in the browser with nothing installed and no key: an 'On this device (beta)' engine in Split soundtrack, and real separation in demo mode. Unverified; ship only if parity and speed hold. Builds on D1 (UI) and D4 (metrics). Read docs/research/dbs-separation-7.md §5 items 4-6 and §11.

STEPS. (1) An export script (scripts/onnx/export_dbs.py, run with the eval venv's torch plus einops, reading the pinned weights) that wraps the network core of DBS-BSRNN and DBS-TIGER: real/imaginary spectrum in, masked spectra out; patch torch.stft/istft and torch.complex (tiger.py L651, L679, L526; modules/dbs.py L315, L332); opset 18 for ScatterElements max; fixed windows (TIGER 517 frames, BSRNN 259) and always-pad, documenting the small difference from the official short-clip path (inference.py L32-34). (2) A parity test against PyTorch on the same input (the pack's test_parity approach; SI-SDR between outputs above a set bar, e.g. 60 dB). (3) JS STFT / iSTFT (n_fft 2048, hop 512, Hann, centre reflect padding) and equal-weight overlap-add with the official windows in src/lib/av/dbs-web/, unit-tested against numpy references. (4) onnxruntime-web pinned to an exact version (bundled, or from an allowed CDN), WASM SIMD with threads, WebGPU where its ops work, in a Web Worker with progress and cancel. (5) UI: 'On this device (beta)' in the engine switch for clips up to 60 s, a time estimate measured on the first run, a fallback to the cloud. (6) Demo mode uses it when available.

TESTS. Export parity (Python, eval venv), JS DSP tests, planner tests for the new engine choice. Then typecheck, lint, targeted tests, full vitest.

BROWSER. /audio/split on-device at 1440 px and 390 px, light and dark; the WASM path in headless Chromium; the main thread stays responsive (worker).

VERIFY HERE. Export and parity run on CPU in the eval venv; WASM inference runs in the headless browser on a 10 s clip with timing. Not verifiable: WebGPU (no GPU here) and phone performance.

LICENCES (information). The exported ONNX files derive from the Apache-2.0 weights: keep the attribution and NOTICE; onnxruntime-web is MIT; DnR v2 CC BY 4.0 attribution as in D1.
